review_notes:
I read all six proofs in the file (lines 1–140). I checked the local definitions they rely on: `lowDegree`, `lowDegree_mono`, `one_mem_lowDegree`, `coord_mem_lowDegree` and `mul_mem_lowDegree` in EdgeProducts.lean; `colorAverage` (a `Module.End ℝ`) and `colorAverage_mul_invariant` in EdgeMonomials.lean; `candidate_average_eq` and `tableCoordinate` in PartialColorings.lean. I also read the Mathlib lemmas I propose: `Submodule.smul_mem_iff`, `Submodule.span_le`, `Finset.prod_const`/`sum_const` and `Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul` (whose ring argument `R` is explicit).

I found three simplifications. None of the replacements was compiled. Small details may need adjusting: whether `rw` finds the cast-card pattern, or whether a `Submodule.mem_comap` unfolding is needed.

I left the other proofs alone. `list_prod_mem_lowDegree`, `lowDegree_substitute` and `lowDegree_lift` are already short and direct. The case analysis in `colorAverage_monomial_mem` matches the mathematics: an unsatisfiable list, a redundant edge, or a new candidate edge. `colorAverage_recurrence` is mostly calls to named lemmas; only its `hsum` step looked worth changing.

apply Submodule.span_induction (p := fun f _ => colorAverage z f ∈
    lowDegree (tableCoordinate z) d) _ _ _ _ hf
findings.problem: The proof uses a four-case span induction. Three of the cases (zero, add, smul) just repeat the fact that `colorAverage z` is linear. That fact is already built into `Submodule.comap` along a linear map. Only the first case, about generators, carries any mathematical content. The very similar lemma `lowDegree_substitute` in the same file already uses the shorter `Submodule.span_le` pattern.
findings.proposed_change:
Show that the span sits inside the preimage, then apply that to `hf`:
```lean
  have hle : lowDegree Pairing.edgeCoord d ≤
      (lowDegree (tableCoordinate z) d).comap (colorAverage z) := by
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro f ⟨l, hl, rfl⟩
    exact lowDegree_mono _ hl (colorAverage_monomial_mem z l)
  exact hle hf
```
findings.benefit: The proof shrinks to its one real idea: each generating monomial maps into low degree. This uses `colorAverage_monomial_mem` together with `lowDegree_mono`. The three linearity cases disappear. The proof now has the same shape as `lowDegree_substitute`, so a reader sees one pattern in both places.

It then cleans up with `smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀ hD, one_smul`. All of this does one step: if `D ≠ 0`, then `D • x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ p`. Mathlib has a lemma for exactly this.

findings.problem: The `hsum` step shows that a sum of equal terms equals card • term. It uses a two-step `calc`. The second step checks the claim one point at a time with `funext M` and an unrestricted `simp`, which hides that this is just the sum-of-a-constant identity plus a cast from nsmul to a real scalar.
findings.proposed_change:
Use the named lemmas directly:
```lean
  have hsum : (∑ f ∈ S, colorAverage z (Pairing.edgeMonomial (f::l))) =
      (S.card : ℝ) • colorAverage z (Pairing.edgeMonomial (e::l)) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun f hf => candidate_average_eq z l _ f e hf he,
      Finset.sum_const, Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℝ]
```
findings.benefit: Each rewrite is one named step: every term equals the average at `e`, a constant sum is card • constant, and the nsmul becomes a real scalar. This makes the structure clearer than an unrestricted `simp` after `funext`. It also removes the unneeded double cast `((S.card : ℕ) : ℝ)`.
